description: PROC MEANS / SUMMARY defaults, CLASS/VAR/OUTPUT mapping, and the stacked layout produced by a bare OUTPUT OUT=.

proc_means_defaults.title: PROC MEANS defaults to N/MEAN/STD/MIN/MAX; CLASS -> groupby, sample std (ddof=1).
rule: Default statistics for `PROC MEANS` are N, MEAN, STD, MIN, MAX. Only request what the SAS output shows.
`VAR` lists the analysis variables to aggregate.
`OUTPUT OUT=... MEAN=... / SUM=...` writes an output dataset; reproduce its exact column names.
SAS std is the **sample** standard deviation (ddof=1). Use `df.std()` (pandas default ddof=1), not `ddof=0`.
Without `NWAY`, PROC MEANS emits subtotals for every combination of CLASS levels; with `NWAY` only the fully-crossed cells. Match whichever the baseline has.
The automatic `_TYPE_` and `_FREQ_` columns appear in the OUTPUT dataset -- recreate them only if present in the QC baseline.
pitfalls: Using ddof=0 gives population std and shifts every value away from SAS.
Forgetting NWAY vs subtotal rows changes the row count of the output dataset.

bare_output_stacked.title: A bare OUTPUT OUT= with no stat=name assignments writes a STACKED dataset, one row per statistic.
rule: A bare `output out=summary;` with no `stat=name` assignments writes a **stacked** dataset: columns `_TYPE_ _FREQ_ _STAT_ <vars>`, one **row per statistic**, not one wide row.

Only the base stats appear: **N, MIN, MAX, MEAN, STD** (and SUM if requested), in that row order. Percentiles/MEDIAN listed on the PROC line are **silently dropped** unless given explicit output names.
`_TYPE_` = 0 with no CLASS; `_FREQ_` = the row count fed to PROC MEANS.
pitfalls: Producing one wide row instead of the stacked _STAT_ layout fails structural QC.
Expecting percentiles/median in the output: a bare OUTPUT drops them silently.
